sample.context: A fictional B2B SaaS customer success manager. This is an illustrative work sample, not a customer result.

sourceFacts.text: Managed a portfolio of 32 B2B SaaS accounts representing $2.4 million in annual recurring revenue.

Introduced monthly renewal-risk reviews and account plans. The portfolio renewal rate increased from 88% to 94% during that year; the source does not establish how much of the increase those changes caused.
Replaced ad hoc onboarding handoffs with a 30-day onboarding plan and a shared launch checklist.
Worked with Product and Support to build the onboarding plan and address recurring onboarding blockers.

Fictional resume structure: a generic summary appears first, followed by a Customer Success Manager role in B2B SaaS, two broad experience bullets about renewals and onboarding, and a generic skills line. F1–F4 are supplied background; their specific scope, actions, and outcomes have not yet been added to this resume.

paper.title: Your resume’s opening
paper.body: Customer-focused professional with strong communication skills and experience helping clients.
paper.compactBody: Customer-focused professional with strong communication skills and experience helping clients.

read.title: Your opening hides your actual specialty
read.body: This opening could fit almost any client-facing role. Your actual story is customer success: owning a SaaS portfolio, reviewing renewal risk, and improving onboarding. Bring that into view before the generic traits.
read.compactBody: The opening hides your work in portfolio ownership, renewals, and onboarding.

next.title: Lead with your actual specialty.
next.body: Try: “Customer success manager with experience owning a $2.4M SaaS portfolio, reviewing renewal risk, and improving onboarding with Product and Support.” Then use the experience section to show the evidence.
next.compactBody: Customer success manager with SaaS portfolio, renewal-risk, and onboarding experience.

modes.label: Impact
modes.question: Does the scale of your work come through?
modes.sourceExcerpt: Responsible for managing customer relationships and renewals.
modes.sourceContext: Experience · the first bullet under Customer Success Manager
modes.integrityNote: The 88% to 94% renewal change is observed over one year. Neither full nor compact advice attributes the entire increase to the candidate’s risk reviews.

paper.title: The first experience point
paper.body: Responsible for managing customer relationships and renewals.
paper.compactBody: Responsible for managing customer relationships and renewals.

read.title: The responsibility is clear. Its scale is missing.
read.body: The line names a duty but leaves out its scale and the observed result. Your background supports 32 accounts, $2.4M ARR, and a renewal rate that rose from 88% to 94%. None of that evidence is visible here.
read.compactBody: 32 accounts. $2.4M ARR. Renewals from 88% to 94%. The scale and result are missing.

next.title: Add the evidence without overstating cause
next.body: Try: “Managed 32 B2B SaaS accounts ($2.4M ARR) and introduced monthly risk reviews. Portfolio renewal rate rose from 88% to 94% that year.” Report the change; don’t claim the reviews alone caused it.
next.compactBody: Managed 32 B2B SaaS accounts ($2.4M ARR). Introduced monthly risk reviews; portfolio renewal rate rose from 88% to 94% that year.

modes.integrityNote: Portfolio ownership, risk reviews, and onboarding are supported by F1–F4. Mid-market experience is unverified and must not be added as a candidate fact. No fit score or hiring prediction is implied.

read.title: You have the examples. The connection needs work.
read.body: The role asks for portfolio ownership, renewal risk, and onboarding. Your facts cover all three. This line shows only onboarding; the other experience point leaves ownership and risk work vague. The account segment is unverified.
read.compactTitle: The work fits. The segment is unverified.
read.compactBody: Portfolio ownership, risk reviews, and onboarding are supported. Mid-market experience needs confirmation.

next.title: Connect your evidence to the role.
next.body: Try: “Owned a 32-account SaaS portfolio, introduced monthly renewal-risk reviews, and built a 30-day onboarding plan with Product and Support.” These examples address the work in the role. Confirm the account segment before claiming mid-market experience.
next.compactBody: Owned a SaaS portfolio, reviewed renewal risk, and built a 30-day onboarding plan with Product and Support.
next.compactNote: Confirm the account segment before adding “mid-market.”
